analyticalQuestion: Does preserving the exact charge-degree lattice remove the apparent large-positive-charge failure near r=0.377, and which genuine input column becomes limiting afterward?
supportedClaim: For the reduced canonical edge generating system with kappa=3/4, retaining each exact i-dependent minimum-degree factor inside the complete convex endpoint sum gives 239 fixed-charge all-degree theorems for 2<=s<241. Exact even and odd rational functions of y=1/s, together with degree-318 strict Bernstein derivative-sign certificates on their full intervals, cover every s>=241. At r=94233/250000 the complete tail bound is 0.9999973490826196656 and the fixed-point and canonical-stretch gates pass. At r=376933/1000000 the true s=162,j=81 column is 1.0000026584572409359, so this specific induced two-block weighted-l1 sufficient inequality fails without implying a singularity or failure of another norm.
